summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV/AIDS, and recent MRSA bacteremia presented with persistent right groin and thigh pain following placement of a new tunneled femoral dialysis catheter. She had no signs of infection or deep vein thrombosis on exam or imaging. The pain was attributed to local scar tissue formation. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 0.9, and warfarin dosing was adjusted. She remained on IV vancomycin for ongoing treatment of recent MRSA bacteremia, with negative surveillance cultures. Headache resolved spontaneously. She was discharged to an extended care facility to complete antibiotics with follow-up planned for anticoagulation management, HIV care, and symptom monitoring.
problems: Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
